starter-drive-assembly.summary: A constrained fork-and-slot linkage connects the provisional solenoid stroke to the sliding clutch and ten-tooth pinion.
starter-drive-assembly.limits: Factory architecture supports a fork lever and drive assembly, but not these dimensions or detailed joint construction. The30/32mm arms, slotted clevis, spherical pads and annular shift groove are provisional. Prescribed CAD motion is not a force, wear, tooth-blocking or starting-sequence simulation. The overrunning clutch interior and transmission-side mounting support remain absent.

steps.title: Accommodate the upper arc
steps.text: The upper pin follows the rotating lever rather than translating in a straight line. A transverse slot in the plunger clevis permits its lateral movement while maintaining the solenoid axis.

steps.title: Shift through the fork
steps.text: Two integral spherical fork pads contact the axial faces of the clutch's annular shift groove. They slide laterally within the groove as the lever rotates; this construction is a candidate solution, not a verified production detail.

steps.title: Retain torque coupling
steps.text: The clutch sleeve translates on the existing provisional shaft splines. A12mm drive stroke corresponds to11.25mm plunger travel with the assumed arm lengths.

steps.title: Reach the ring and reset
steps.text: The pinion advances from3.525mm axial clearance to8.475mm overlap with the indexed manual flywheel. Reversing the prescribed fraction restores the resting geometry; real spring forces and tooth-blocking are not modeled.

steps.title: Keep the freewheel boundary
steps.text: A real overrunning clutch prevents the running engine from overspeeding the starter armature. The displayed clutch is still an envelope and sliding interface, not a functioning internal one-way mechanism.

troubleshooting.title: Do not confuse clearance with service fit
troubleshooting.text: Sampled interference checks establish only the candidate's geometry. They do not verify production bellhousing depth, clutch function, tooth engagement under load or safe electrical performance.
